strengths: Well-motivated problem distinguishing instance-level query circuits from global capability circuits

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets (IOI, arithmetic, MMLU 9 categories, ARC) with ablations and scaling studies

Extensive supplementary experiments and honest discussion of limitations
weaknesses: Core methodological contribution is limited: BoN is a straightforward engineering heuristic (generate paraphrases, select best circuit), not a principled algorithmic advance; feels incremental rather than fundamental

strengths: Clear problem formulation distinguishing query circuits from capability circuits with well-motivated practical applications
Thorough identification and empirical validation of technical challenges (NFS instability, method degradation, high edge budgets)

Creative BoN sampling approach grounded in the insightful observation that circuits can succeed on paraphrases when failing on originals
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple benchmarks (IOI, arithmetic, MMLU, ARC) with rigorous ablations and statistical testing
Strong empirical results: circuits using only 1.3% of edges recover ~60% performance on MMLU, validated across larger models
Evidence of circuit interpretability: shared sub-circuit analysis (Figure 8) demonstrates circuits capture common mechanisms rather than random solutions

weaknesses: BoN lacks rigorous theoretical justification: why paraphrases specifically alleviate gradient noise remains hand-wavy; alternative perturbation methods (BoN-GP, BoN-Random) show potential but comparative analysis is incomplete
